CAMEL-24973.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) silent security fix found via GitHub repo sweep (commit 84f265e8d1b3548fd03f0fd0474cf6c410e5e9e6, PR #26803, merged 2026-09-25T09:19:50Z): three call sites built endpoint-configuration error messages ('Unknown parameters=[...]') by directly interpolating the raw options Map into the exception message with zero masking -- org.apache.camel.support.DefaultComponent.validateParameters() and org.apache.camel.support.ScheduledPollConsumer (both camel-support, used_component) plus camel-jetty's JettyHttpComponent12 (not used). Any sensitive option name Camel doesn't recognise (typo, wrong case, wrong dash form) that also carries a secret value (e.g. privateKeyPassphrase, password, accessKey) would have its plaintext value written straight into a thrown ResolveEndpointFailedException message -- CWE-532 (insertion of sensitive information into log file / exception trace). Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag that both used-component call sites contain the identical unmasked pattern unchanged (DefaultComponent.java:305 'Unknown parameters=[" + param + "]'; ScheduledPollConsumer.java:660 '... + copy + ...', both with no URISupport.sanitizeParameters() or equivalent call -- that method does not exist in 4.8.8) and that 4.8.8's existing URI-level sanitizer (URISupport.sanitizeUri's ALL_SECRETS regex) could not mask this leak anyway, since it requires a '?'/'&'-prefixed query-string key and a bare Map.toString() has neither. -> AFFECTS_US. Severity MEDIUM (estimated): requires an attacker/operator-supplied endpoint URI with an unrecognised parameter name carrying a sensitive value, and for the resulting exception message to reach a log or an exposed error response. Fix does NOT apply cleanly to 4.8.8 -- upstream ships it as part of a much larger URISupport/SensitiveUtils rewrite (137+152 changed lines introducing new isSensitiveKey/MASK/sanitizeParameters helpers and a rewritten userinfo-masking engine) that 4.8.8 does not have the surrounding scaffolding for. Recommended minimal backport: add a small local sanitizeParameters(Map) helper in our fork that reuses 4.8.8's existing SensitiveUtils.getSensitivePattern() to mask matching keys' values, and call it at the two used-component call sites (DefaultComponent.java:305, ScheduledPollConsumer.java:660) instead of porting the full upstream refactor. Upstream has also already backported the full fix to the 4.22.x branch (PR #26895) if a closer reference implementation is wanted. See reports/2026-09-26.md.

CAMEL-25106.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) silent security fix found via full commit sweep of the incremental window (commit 7057526605849e02dfc85b83ef3223abef238650, PR #27010, merged 2026-09-28): camel-kafka's KafkaConfiguration.createProducerProperties()/createConsumerProperties() applied sslContextParameters (setting ssl.keystore.*/ssl.truststore.*/etc.) but never touched security.protocol, which stays at its field default CommonClientConfigs.DEFAULT_SECURITY_PROTOCOL='PLAINTEXT' unless the user ALSO explicitly sets securityProtocol=SSL. Kafka's own client ignores all ssl.* properties under security.protocol=PLAINTEXT, so an endpoint configured with only sslContextParameters silently opens a completely unencrypted, unauthenticated socket to the broker -- CWE-319 (cleartext transmission of sensitive info), effectively also CWE-295 (no cert validation occurs at all under plaintext). camel-kafka IS a used_component. Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag (components/camel-kafka/.../KafkaConfiguration.java lines 315, 410-417 and the consumer-side equivalent) that the identical pattern (sslContextParameters applied, but securityProtocol left at its PLAINTEXT default, never auto-upgraded) exists unchanged -> AFFECTS_US. Severity HIGH (estimated). Recommend an IMMEDIATE config audit (independent of any code fix): grep our route/application configs for sslContextParameters set on any kafka: endpoint/component without an explicit securityProtocol=SSL/SASL_SSL also set -- if that pattern exists in production, traffic is unencrypted today. Fix does not apply cleanly to 4.8.8: upstream also reorders endpoint-option-vs-context SSL precedence (addSslOption() helper), a moderately invasive change; the officially-backported PRs for camel-4.22.x and camel-4.18.x both reportedly hit cherry-pick conflicts, and no 4.8.x port exists or is planned upstream. Minimal in-house backport: add a resolveSecurityProtocol() that upgrades PLAINTEXT->SSL whenever sslContextParameters is set and securityProtocol is still at its default, called right before the existing addPropertyIfNotEmpty(SECURITY_PROTOCOL_CONFIG, ...) line in both createProducerProperties/createConsumerProperties. Port KafkaSslContextParametersTest (new upstream test) alongside. No CVE/GHSA filed as of this run.

CAMEL-24451.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) silent security fix found via full commit sweep (commit e65fd915f6fd0be99da1186216a79a65104149cb, closes PR #26904, merged 2026-09-28): camel-xslt's XsltUriResolver.resolve() (invoked when an XSLT stylesheet calls the document() XPath function at transform time) resolved http:/https:/ftp:/file: URIs completely unconditionally, with zero protocol/URI restriction -- confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag that the pre-fix XsltUriResolver has no access check anywhere. JAXP's ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET TransformerFactory attribute (the standard defense) is only enforced when no custom URIResolver returns a Source -- but Camel's XsltBuilder always installs its own resolver, silently bypassing that hardening even on deployments (e.g. camel-xslt-saxon, or a custom transformerFactory) that explicitly set ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET to restrict external access. Compounding this, XsltBuilder binds every inbound message header as a stylesheet parameter (confirmed at line 480 of 4.8.8's XsltBuilder.java), so an attacker who controls any header on a route ending in an xslt: step, combined with a stylesheet parameter reaching document(), can direct the transform to fetch an internal URL (SSRF, CWE-918) or read a local file (file:///etc/passwd, arbitrary file read, CWE-73) and have the result merged into transform output. camel-xslt IS a used_component -> AFFECTS_US. Severity HIGH (estimated), contingent on whether ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET hardening is/was assumed in place (plain camel-xslt never sets it itself, so a fully-default JAXP TransformerFactory was already at risk independent of this Camel bug; this fix specifically closes the gap for deployments relying on hardening via camel-xslt-saxon or a custom transformerFactory). Immediate mitigation regardless of backport timing: configure a hardened TransformerFactory (or JVM-wide javax.xml.accessExternalStylesheet/accessExternalDTD system properties) and strip/allow-list headers before any xslt: step whose stylesheet uses document() with a parameter. Backport: patch is self-contained to XsltBuilder.java/XsltUriResolver.java in components/camel-xslt; 4.8.8's constructor/resolve() signature is close enough that the new checkExternalAccessAllowed/parseAllowedProtocols logic should port with minor adaptation. Port XsltUriResolverExternalAccessTest. No 4.8.x backport label upstream; ships first in unreleased main (4.23.0).

CAMEL-25017.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) silent security fix found via full commit sweep (commit ab21f790a87d3483f6be23dd4b8150a8dc62e3e4, PR #26882, merged 2026-09-28): Claim Check EIP's ClaimCheckProcessor.getClaimCheckRepository() lazily creates a DefaultClaimCheckRepository (a plain non-thread-safe HashMap/Deque) and stores it as an ordinary exchange property. Camel's Splitter/Multicast/Recipient List/Wire Tap EIPs (and SEDA/Disruptor queue hand-off) shallow-copy the properties map when duplicating an Exchange, so every copy ends up holding a reference to the SAME repository object -- with parallelProcessing(), concurrent split branches then read/write the same HashMap/Deque. Upstream's own upgrade-guide note: 'with parallel processing a Get or Pop could return the message of another part.' A realistic pattern: a split().parallelProcessing() route where each branch claim-checks a different record/customer payload under the same literal key -- one branch's Get/Pop can retrieve a DIFFERENT branch's claimed-away exchange (headers+body), i.e. cross-message data leakage/corruption between concurrently processed parts of a batch (CWE-362 race condition -> CWE-200 information exposure). camel-core IS a used_component (Claim Check EIP ships in camel-core-processor). Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag: DefaultClaimCheckRepository.java implements ClaimCheckRepository only (no safe-copy mechanism), ClaimCheckProcessor.java stores the repo via plain exchange.setProperty() identical to pre-fix main, and AbstractExchange.copy()/ExchangeHelper.copyExchangeWithProperties() only special-case MESSAGE_HISTORY, with zero handling for the claim-check repository -> all vulnerable code paths present verbatim -> AFFECTS_US. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH (estimated). Fix applies cleanly: diffed all three touch points (AbstractExchange.copy() in camel-support, ExchangeHelper in camel-support, PooledProcessorExchangeFactory in camel-base-engine, plus DefaultClaimCheckRepository/ClaimCheckProcessor in camel-core-processor) against 4.8.8 line-by-line -- surrounding code matches exactly in every case, no drift. Port ClaimCheckEipSplitParallelTest, ClaimCheckEipStoreCopyTest, PooledExchangeClaimCheckEipSplitParallelTest. No CVE/GHSA filed; recommend prioritizing given camel-core is our most heavily used module and split+parallelProcessing+claim-check is a plausible production batch-pipeline pattern.

CAMEL-24650.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) silent security fix found via full commit sweep (commit 0099984f836579b0ca53f95ff81f7870cd7e24eb, PR #26872, merged 2026-09-28): camel-http-common's DefaultHttpBinding.populateAttachments() checked an uploaded multipart file's extension against the configured fileNameExtWhitelist using `!fileNameExtWhitelist.contains(ext)` -- a SUBSTRING match, not a whitelist-entry match. With a whitelist such as 'html,htm,txt,csv,pdf,doc,docx,xls,xlsx', a crafted short extension that happens to be a substring of any allowed entry (e.g. 'ls' is contained in 'xls', 'oc' in 'doc', 'ml' in 'html') is incorrectly ACCEPTED even though it was never actually whitelisted -- CWE-434 (unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type) via extension-whitelist bypass. Note camel-servlet/camel-jetty's own AttachmentHttpBinding subclasses already had a correct exact-match implementation from an earlier fix (CAMEL-24427); this bug is specifically in DefaultHttpBinding's own separate, older, buggy copy, used by any HTTP-server component built directly on camel-http-common without a jetty/servlet-specific override. camel-http-common IS a used_component. Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag (components/camel-http-common/.../DefaultHttpBinding.java line 339): the exact vulnerable substring-match code `if (!fileNameExtWhitelist.equals("*") && !fileNameExtWhitelist.contains(ext))` is present verbatim, and HttpCommonEndpoint instantiates DefaultHttpBinding directly as the default binding -> AFFECTS_US. Severity MEDIUM (estimated) -- depends on which HTTP-server component(s) built on camel-http-common we run without a servlet/jetty-specific attachment binding override, and whether fileNameExtWhitelist is configured at all (default is permissive '*', in which case this bug is moot -- only relevant if an explicit whitelist is configured for a component using the base DefaultHttpBinding). Backport applies cleanly: self-contained method replacement (isFileNameAccepted) inside DefaultHttpBinding.java; 4.8.8's surrounding populateAttachments code matches closely. Port DefaultHttpBindingTest's testFileNameAcceptedDoesNotMatchSubstring regression test.

CAMEL-25023.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) silent security fix found via full commit sweep (commit d51cc4c98a9fe98f2c5c7d148eea0d5526445fb3, closes PR #26892, merged 2026-09-28): camel-util's IOHelper.copy(InputStream, OutputStream, int bufferSize, boolean flushOnEachWrite, long maxSize) -- the shared size-limit-enforcing copy routine behind decompression-bomb guards such as camel-zipfile's maxDecompressedSize -- accumulated the running byte count in an `int total` while comparing it against the already-long `maxSize`. Once the cumulative sum itself overflows past Integer.MAX_VALUE (~2.147 GiB) during int arithmetic, `total` wraps to a negative value, and a negative int compared against a large positive maxSize is always false -- the size check silently stops firing forever above ~2 GiB, for any maxDecompressedSize configured at 2 GiB or higher. CWE-190 (integer overflow) enabling CWE-409/CWE-400 (decompression bomb / uncontrolled resource consumption). The default maxDecompressedSize (1 GiB) is below the wrap point and unaffected; only deployments that have explicitly raised the limit lose all protection above ~2 GiB. camel-util IS a used_component, and camel-zipfile (also a used_component, config/libraries.yaml line 92) calls IOHelper.copy(..., maxSize) via ZipFileDataFormat/ZipIterator to enforce maxDecompressedSize. Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag (core/camel-util/.../IOHelper.java line 241 `int total = 0;`, lines 260-261 `total += n; if (maxSize > 0 && total > maxSize) throw ...`) that the byte-for-byte identical vulnerable pattern is present -> AFFECTS_US. Severity MEDIUM (estimated) -- exposure is currently theoretical unless our config sets maxDecompressedSize >= 2 GiB on camel-zipfile/camel-tarfile (recommend auditing this). Backport applies cleanly: trivial, self-contained local-variable-type change (int -> long accumulator, capped return); no signature change. Port IOHelperTest's testCopyMaxSizeOfTwoGigabytesOrMore/testCopyMoreThanTwoGigabytes (use a synthetic zero-input-stream, no multi-GB allocation needed) -- cheap enough to backport proactively even without confirming current exposure.

CAMEL-25104.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) silent security fix found via full commit sweep (commit 3e7c7cd0d997bd8c6e872e10aa704a60f79a55d9, PR #27008, merged 2026-09-28): camel-core's BaseSSLContextParameters ships two hard-coded default filters applied whenever a user does not configure explicit cipher-suite/protocol filters: DEFAULT_CIPHER_SUITES_FILTER_EXCLUDE (pre-fix: no 3DES pattern, only NULL/anon/EXPORT/DES/MD5/RC4) and DEFAULT_SECURE_SOCKET_PROTOCOLS_FILTER_EXCLUDE (pre-fix: 'SSL.*' only, does not exclude TLSv1/TLSv1.1). Separately, the SSLServerSocket configurer computed its 'available values' universe from socket.getSupportedCipherSuites()/getSupportedProtocols() (the JDK's full raw-supported list, which includes suites/protocols the JVM's own jdk.tls.disabledAlgorithms security policy already excludes from its enabled-by-default set) instead of the already-hardened getSSLParameters() form that the SSLEngine/SSLSocket configurers correctly use. Net effect: Camel's own default filtering can silently re-widen the effective negotiable protocol/cipher set beyond what the JVM itself would otherwise enable by default (legacy TLSv1/TLSv1.1 and 3DES/Sweet32-vulnerable ciphers remain negotiable), purely from Camel's own filtering, with zero user configuration involved -- CWE-757 (selection of less-secure algorithm during negotiation), CWE-327 (use of a broken/risky crypto algorithm, 3DES/Sweet32). camel-core IS a used_component. Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag (core/camel-api/.../jsse/BaseSSLContextParameters.java lines 61-68): identical pre-fix filter lists, and the SSLServerSocket configurer (lines ~599-628) still calls getSupportedCipherSuites()/getSupportedProtocols() -- the SSLEngine/SSLSocket configurers in 4.8.8 already use getSSLParameters(), so the 'supported vs enabled' defect is scoped only to the SSLServerSocket path in both versions -> AFFECTS_US. Severity MEDIUM (estimated). Backport applies cleanly: same file/package in both trees, identical surrounding code, the upstream ~12-line diff should apply with at most trivial offset. Port SSLContextParametersDefaultProtocolsTest. Fix ships in 4.23.0 (main); PR requests backports for 4.22.x and 4.18.x -- no port/camel-4.8.x label exists, 4.8.8 needs a manual backport.

CAMEL-24756.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) silent security fix found via full commit sweep (commit 92f6f789ff0cac3e05da3da710b8e26fb9d69325, PR #26734, merged 2026-09-28): camel-base-engine's DefaultResourceResolvers.HttpResource (used for http:/https: resource: locations, e.g. loading routes, schemas, or scripts from a remote URL) opened its URLConnection with neither setConnectTimeout nor setReadTimeout, and the JDK default for both is 0 (wait forever). Resource resolution typically happens on the bootstrap thread during CamelContext startup, so a remote server that accepts the TCP connection and then never responds (or responds with an extremely slow trickle) hangs startup indefinitely -- CWE-400 (uncontrolled resource consumption) / availability impact via unbounded hang, with attacker relevance wherever the http: resource location is influenced by external/dynamic input (e.g. a header- or property-driven resource: URI) rather than a fixed, trusted, operator-authored location. camel-base-engine IS a used_component. Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag (core/camel-base-engine/.../DefaultResourceResolvers.java): no setConnectTimeout/setReadTimeout call exists anywhere in HttpResource -> the identical unbounded-wait pattern is present -> AFFECTS_US. Severity LOW-MEDIUM (estimated) -- real but narrow: exploitability depends on an http(s): resource location being reachable with attacker-influenced or attacker-controlled input, which is not the common case for this mechanism. Fix adds connect/read timeouts (10s/30s defaults, overridable via camel.resource.http.connect-timeout / camel.resource.http.read-timeout system properties, 0 restores prior behavior). Backport applies cleanly: self-contained addition to DefaultResourceResolvers.java, no signature change to existing public API (only the internal HttpResource construction call sites change). No test class mentioned by name in the commit beyond upgrade-guide notes; add a basic connect/read-timeout unit test if backporting.

CAMEL-25089.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) fix found via full commit sweep (commit c7f696b9e08f3699dd7c4ae7840e564f57573bd1, PR #26990, merged 2026-09-28): camel-file's FileLockClusterView.doStop() released the OS file lock (and thus allowed another cluster member to become leader) WITHOUT first telling local listeners (notably ClusteredRoutePolicy, which starts/stops managed routes based on leadership) that this member had lost leadership -- fireLeadershipChangedEvent(null) was missing from the stop path entirely. This creates a window during graceful shutdown/redeploy/scale-down where a NEW leader can start its managed routes while the OLD leader's ClusteredRoutePolicy-managed routes haven't yet been told to stop -- two members briefly both actively running the same clustered route (e.g. both reading/processing the same files if using camel-file's FileLockClusterView), risking duplicate processing / data-integrity issues rather than a classic auth/injection vulnerability. camel-cluster IS a used_component. Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag: FileLockClusterView.doStop() calls only closeInternal() (lock.release()) with no fireLeadershipChangedEvent call anywhere in the stop path -> the same missing-notification defect class is present. Marked NEEDS_REVIEW rather than AFFECTS_US because the practical blast radius depends on whether our deployment actually uses camel-file's FileLockClusterView for clustering (vs. another cluster-service implementation) and on route idempotency under brief duplicate processing. Severity LOW-MEDIUM (estimated). If confirmed relevant, backport is a small, targeted addition (insert the wasLeader-gated fireLeadershipChangedEvent(null) call before the lock/data-file release in FileLockClusterView.doStop()) -- 4.8.8's doStop()/closeInternal() shape is simple enough that this should port with minimal adaptation. No CVE/GHSA filed.

CAMEL-25063.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) fix found via full commit sweep (commit 80dd201302eaffde681e37b56b9f3a117c3cae12, PR #26946, merged 2026-09-28): camel-management's ManagedCamelContext/ManagedRoute escapeXml() helper (used when serializing route/context statistics to XML via dumpRouteAsXml/dumpRoutesAsXml/dumpStepStatsAsXml, reachable via JMX MBean operations) only escaped &, <, > and NOT the double-quote character, even though the escaped strings (route id, route group, and critically sourceLocation -- which pre-fix was not even passed through escapeXml at all, using the raw getSourceLocation() value) are interpolated directly into XML ATTRIBUTE values (e.g. sourceLocation="%s"). A route id/group/source-location string containing a literal double-quote could break out of the attribute and inject additional XML attributes/structure into the dumped XML -- CWE-91-adjacent (XML injection). Practical exploitability is narrow: it requires an attacker (or an untrusted upstream) to control a route id or a route's source-location string (typically developer/deployment-controlled, not end-user input at runtime) and a downstream consumer of the dumped XML that parses it naively/trusts well-formedness (e.g. a management UI or CI tool ingesting dumpRoutesAsXml output). Also fixed in the same commit: a JMX-wildcard route-id-matching bug in reset(true) (used Query.match() instead of Query.eq(), so a route id containing literal * or ? could reset stats of unrelated routes -- a blast-radius/correctness issue for an already-authorized JMX caller, not a privilege escalation). camel-management IS a used_component. Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag: ManagedRoute.java interpolates raw getSourceLocation() into sourceLocation="%s" with NO escapeXml call at all (lines 546, 615, 667, 677) -- our pinned version has an even less-escaped form of this pattern than pre-fix main. Marked NEEDS_REVIEW rather than AFFECTS_US because exploitability hinges on an untrusted-input path into route ids/source locations that we have not confirmed exists in our deployment, and on a downstream XML consumer that doesn't tolerate malformed/injected XML. Severity LOW (estimated). If confirmed relevant, backport is straightforward: switch to a quote-escaping helper (upstream uses StringHelper.xmlEncode) and apply it to sourceLocation everywhere it's interpolated. No CVE/GHSA filed.

CAMEL-25057.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) fix found via full commit sweep (commit b4073ca92553cfe68af02e22c21c1dff9f7a3a40, PR #26940, merged 2026-09-28): camel-console's TraceDevConsole gated dumping ALL backlog-traced message content (bodies/headers -- potentially sensitive business data) on `if (dump != null)`, i.e. any non-null value of the dump query/option parameter -- including the literal string 'false' -- triggered a full trace-content dump. Fixed to require `"true".equalsIgnoreCase(dump)`. A caller who passed dump=false (or any other non-null value) intending to SUPPRESS the dump would instead receive it. camel-console IS a used_component. Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag: TraceDevConsole.java has `if (dump != null)` at both call sites (lines 79, 137) -- the same over-triggering behavior is present. Marked NEEDS_REVIEW rather than a clear vulnerability because this doesn't add or remove any authentication/authorization -- dev-console access is already gated the same way regardless of the dump= value, and dumping trace content on this console (for an already-authorized caller) is its intended purpose; the bug only changes WHICH query values trigger the dump, not WHO can trigger it. Real-world impact requires an authorized-but-careless caller (or integration) that passes a dump= value other than 'true' while expecting no dump. Severity LOW (estimated). Backport straightforward if desired: change the guard to an equalsIgnoreCase('true') check at both call sites. No CVE/GHSA filed.

CAMEL-25084.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE/GHSA yet) fix found via full commit sweep (commit d954046aace20f25ee9d654bd6590c6a057b86f0, PR #26984, merged 2026-09-28): among a broad batch of camel-util string/time/URI/file helper correctness fixes, one touches FileUtil.compactPath()'s '..'-collapsing stack logic: pre-fix, encountering '..' when the stack held only a single Windows drive-letter entry (e.g. 'C:') would POP that drive-letter entry too (no guard against popping below a drive root), producing a malformed compacted path that has lost its drive prefix. compactPath() is the function GenericFileProducer.jailedCheck() (camel-file's core path-traversal containment check -- 'file must be within starting directory') calls on BOTH the candidate answer and the baseDir before comparing them with GenericFileHelper.isWithinDirectory(). camel-util and camel-file (via camel-file's use of FileUtil.compactPath, confirmed by grep across components/camel-file) are used_components. On manual trace-through of a Windows-drive baseDir scenario (e.g. baseDir='C:\\data', a crafted answer walking '..' past the drive root), the over-popping appears to produce a compacted answer that no longer starts with the compacted baseDir -- i.e. the containment check would likely still REJECT (fail closed) rather than being bypassed, so this looks more like a correctness/confusing-error-message bug than a proven jail-check bypass. However this has NOT been proven safe with an actual reproduction/test on a Windows-path baseDir configuration, and jailedCheck is the same defense class as the already-tracked CAMEL-24419 (AFFECTS_US) finding, so it warrants a closer look rather than an outright dismissal. Confirmed via direct source read of the camel-4.8.8 tag that FileUtil.compactPath() has the identical pre-fix stack logic with no Windows-drive guard (core/camel-util/.../FileUtil.java); note 4.8.8's separate FileUtil.normalizePath() is a trivial, unrelated separator-conversion function (not the vulnerable one -- do not confuse the two). Severity LOW (estimated) pending confirmation. If backported: the guard is a small, self-contained addition (isWindowsDrive() check) to compactPath()'s stack-processing loop. No CVE/GHSA filed. This project only runs camel-file on Linux/container hosts in practice (Windows-drive paths would not arise) -- recommend confirming that assumption before spending further effort here.

CAMEL-25105.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE) security fix found via full commit sweep (commit 960f69708939a9c921c38383ce3e0b7dde78a4a9, PR #27009, merged 2026-09-28): camel-netty's DefaultServerInitializerFactory/HttpServerInitializerFactory unconditionally called engine.setNeedClientAuth(consumer.getConfiguration().isNeedClientAuth()) AFTER an SSLEngine already configured via sslContextParameters' clientAuthentication=REQUIRE had need-client-auth set -- silently disabling a configured mutual-TLS requirement whenever the separate, Netty-specific needClientAuth endpoint option (default false) wasn't ALSO set to true. CAMEL-25103.note: SUSPECTED (no CVE) security fix found via full commit sweep (commit 0a541d75d6231c2f76002ab9eacb6b7548112f73, PR #27007, merged 2026-09-28): camel-vertx's VertxHelper.setupSSLOptions() (shared by camel-platform-http-vertx/camel-vertx-http/camel-vertx-websocket) never read sslContextParameters' clientAuthentication setting nor its effective cipher/protocol filters -- configuring REQUIRE client-auth or cipher/protocol restrictions had zero effect on Vert.x-based endpoints, a full silent bypass of intended mTLS enforcement and cipher/protocol hardening.
